name: Animation & Illustration
shortDescription: Medical animation and illustration for cardiology and medical device companies: mechanism of action (MoA) animation, procedure walk-throughs, 3D model development, medical illustration and infographics.
whyThisMatters:
Medical device animation shows how a device works inside the body, from its mechanism of action to each step of the procedure, in a way live footage and slides cannot.

Physicians are sceptical, cath lab teams are busy and hospital buyers need the value case in plain terms. A clear animation answers the questions each of them has, and keeps working long after launch: on the stand, in a sales meeting, in training and on social channels.

We combine medical accuracy with craft. Our animations are built with the KOLs who use the device, checked against the clinical evidence, and made to pass medical, legal and regulatory review. We use 3D, 2D and stop-motion, whichever tells the story best, and pair them with filmed procedures and interviews when the story needs both.

process.title: Brief and evidence
process.text: We start from the clinical evidence, the instructions for use and the imaging, and agree the one thing each audience must understand.

process.title: Script and storyboard
process.text: We write and storyboard with your KOLs and medical team, so the science is right before a single frame is made.

process.title: Design and animate
process.text: Style frames, then 3D, 2D or stop-motion animation, with anatomy and device details checked at every stage.

process.title: Review and deliver
process.text: Built for medical, legal and regulatory review, then delivered in the cuts, formats and languages your teams need.

faqs.question: What is a mechanism of action (MoA) animation?
faqs.answer: It is an animation that shows how a medical device or therapy works inside the body: how it is delivered, what it does to the tissue or vessel, and why that leads to a better outcome. For medical device companies it is often the clearest way to explain what makes a product different.

faqs.question: What kinds of medical animation do you make?
faqs.answer: Mechanism of action animations, step-by-step procedure guides, device explainers and value stories for hospital administrators, in 3D, 2D or stop-motion. For iVascular we filmed the Angiolite stent expanding inside life-sized transparent artery models, using stop-motion to show its growth frame by frame.

faqs.question: How do you make sure the animation is medically accurate?
faqs.answer: We work from the clinical evidence and instructions for use, script and storyboard with the KOLs who use the device, and check anatomy and device detail at every stage. Each animation is built to go through medical, legal and regulatory review.

faqs.question: Can an animation be used to train physicians and cath lab staff?
faqs.answer: Yes. For Philips we produced a medical-grade animation of the end-to-end use of the VeriSight Pro ICE catheter in the LAAO procedure, a step-by-step guide for physicians, radiographers and cath lab staff.

faqs.question: Do you combine animation with filmed procedures and interviews?
faqs.answer: Often. Animation explains what cannot be filmed; live procedures and KOL interviews add credibility. Many of our campaigns, including our work for Philips, Medtronic and iVascular, combine the two.

faqs.question: Can the animation be versioned for different markets?
faqs.answer: Yes. We plan for cut-downs, formats and languages from the start, so one animation can serve congress booths, sales teams, training and social channels in each market you sell in.

faqs.question: Can you build 3D models of our device and anatomy?
faqs.answer: Yes. We build anatomically accurate 3D models from device CAD and clinical references, including real-time 3D for VR and interactive tools, with device deployment animated step by step and checked against the clinical case.

faqs.question: Can animation be combined with live action?
faqs.answer: Yes. We composite animation, imaging and data visualisations into filmed scenes, tracked to camera, and use kinetic typography and motion graphics to bring evidence on screen.
